briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Today's climate briefing for October 21, 2026, will now begin.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis: Accelerating Alarms
sections.content: International news collected today strongly warns that the impacts of climate change are accelerating across the globe. Leading climate scientists have stated that global warming is accelerating [53]. Indeed, in California, a record-breaking rainy winter is anticipated due to the convergence of climate change and a Super El Niño [52, 54, 59, 97], and threats to Humboldt Bay from sea-level rise have also been reported [95]. Furthermore, climate change is increasing gun violence incidents in the U.S. [61], and doctors in 136 countries are already reporting climate change impacts appearing on patients' skin [98], indicating that multifaceted threats are becoming a reality.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Climate Change Impacts and Response Challenges
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change observed both domestically and internationally present serious challenges to our daily lives and economy. In France, an unprecedented climate change heatwave led to student protests [1], and in our seas, the National Institute of Fisheries Science warned that high-temperature phenomena have become commonplace [2]. Meanwhile, the incident of a Florida governor's statue melting is interpreted as a strong warning against policies that ignore the climate crisis [4], and social pressure on policy decisions is growing, as seen with the UK facing climate backlash after approving North Sea gas drilling [105]. Amidst these circumstances, calls to 'halt indiscriminate renewable energy development' [40] and claims that 'a Honam semiconductor cluster is impossible without nuclear power' [44] illustrate the complex reality of energy transition.

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Despite challenging circumstances, domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality are actively unfolding. Domestically, Kookmin University's HUSS Environmental Consortium successfully concluded the '2026 GREEN JOBS Career Camp' [3]. Namyangju City opened a Carbon Neutrality Support Center, establishing a base for achieving greenhouse gas reduction targets [8, 9, 23, 28]. Notably, Gwangmyeong City Mayor Park Seung-won actively proposed to the government the establishment of a national project, 'Carbon Neutrality Leading Local Governments 100' [6, 7, 14, 16, 22, 27, 32, 35], emphasizing the leading role of local governments. The European Union (EU) also affirmed its global commitment to carbon neutrality by finalizing a target to reduce greenhouse gases by 90% by 2040 [45].

sections.title: ⚙️ Renewable Energy and Green Technology: Innovations for the Future
sections.content: Renewable energy and eco-friendly technologies are gaining attention as key drivers for overcoming the climate crisis. Renewable energy experts are playing a crucial role in illuminating the future of advanced industries [36], and Shinsung E&G unveiled cooling and renewable energy solutions for AI data centers [37]. Large-scale renewable energy expansion plans are also taking shape, with the Korea Power Exchange discussing the promotion of a 100GW renewable energy mega-project with the Gwangju Citizens' Organizations Council [42, 48]. Furthermore, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries began operating an oil tanker equipped with the 'Wing Sail' wind-assisted propulsion system [51], leading technological innovation for carbon neutrality in the maritime transport sector.

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Adaptation and Research Trends
sections.content: The international community continues various research and policy discussions to understand and adapt to the impacts of climate change. The California state government released new climate science research findings and predictions to prepare for climate change impacts [54, 93, 97], and scientific understanding is being enhanced through studies of ancient climate change to analyze differences with the present [65]. However, challenges in international cooperation also exist, such as a crucial IPCC meeting held in Ethiopia ending in 'deep disappointment' after failing to agree on a report publication schedule [106]. Alongside arguments that adaptation policies should be established centered around local communities facing climate change [63], practical efforts to strengthen adaptation capabilities are also underway, such as the Ministry of Education opening a Climate Change Action Center [104].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing demonstrates that while the climate crisis is accelerating, various domestic and international efforts and innovations to overcome it coexist. This is a time when continuous scientific research, global cooperation, and practical actions by all stakeholders are becoming even more crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
